risks.description: After a process restart the durable workflow store must re-open and re-derive state; a lost, un-checkpointed WAL or a corrupted DB would silently drop approved workflow state (AC: state survives restart).
risks.basis: AC 'workflow state survives a process restart' (weight 3); callback binds WorkflowStore over workflow.sqlite3 and the checkpoint handle key is per-process/in-memory.

risks.description: A write that fails or is interrupted mid-transaction could leave a partially-applied workflow: a checkpoint witness without its grant, or a run advanced without its audit/ledger row.
risks.basis: AC 'a failed write leaves no partially applied workflow' (weight 3); checkpoint.py asserts witness+grant mint in ONE transaction with 'no partial authorization state'.

risks.description: Rebuilding workflow state from history at startup could re-execute an already-committed effect, producing a second live/CLAIMED grant for the same logical effect (double invoice/write).
risks.basis: AC 'rebuilding state from history never re-executes an effect' (weight 3); ledger relies on ix_effect_grants_live_hold and ix_effect_grants_commit_once for one commitment per (tenant, commit_key).

risks.description: A read after a write could return stale in-process cached state instead of the durable row if any read path still consults the moved-away cache.
risks.basis: AC 'a read after a write never returns stale state' (weight 2); this is the read half of the cache->durable-store move and cannot be exercised without an authored write.

risks.description: If the durable store's schema is not actually the canonical workflow-bearing shape, 'moving state to the durable store' is nominal only and state has no durable home.
risks.basis: AC 'workflow state survives a process restart' (weight 3); schema.py CANONICAL_TABLES must include workflow_runs/effect_grants/checkpoint_witnesses.

scenarios.title: The durable workflow store actually carries the workflow-bearing tables
scenarios.purpose: Prove workflow state has a durable home: building the canonical schema yields the workflow_runs / effect_grants / checkpoint_witnesses tables, so 'moved to the durable store' is structural, not nominal.
scenarios.rationale: If the canonical durable schema does not contain the workflow tables, the whole unit is a no-op; this is the cheapest load-bearing precondition for every restart-survival claim.
scenarios.generating_risk: The state may have been 'moved' to a store that does not actually contain the workflow tables.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-P5-1: workflow state survives a process restart
scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only w.r.t. the repo: the approved probe builds a fresh DB under tempfile.mkdtemp() and prints table names; it touches no shared workspace DB and needs no cleanup.

actions.name: canonical_schema_tables
actions.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import sqlite3,tempfile,os,sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from freight_recon.schema import create_canonical_schema; p=os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(),'probe.sqlite3'); c=sqlite3.connect(p); create_canonical_schema(c); print(sorted(r[0] for r in c.execute(\"select name from sqlite_master where type='table'\")))"

scenarios.title: Durable store re-opens intact and consistent after a clean process restart
scenarios.purpose: Exercise 'state survives a process restart': restart the callback process and confirm the durable DB re-opens, the workflow tables are still present, integrity is intact, and no foreign-key (orphan) violations were introduced.
scenarios.rationale: The unit's headline promise is that restarting the process does not lose or corrupt persisted workflow state; a restart followed by integrity/FK inspection is the direct oracle available without a signer secret.
scenarios.generating_risk: A restart could drop un-flushed state or leave the store corrupted/unreadable.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-P5-1: workflow state survives a process restart
scenarios.isolation_note: Restarts the shared callback service and issues read-only SELECT/PRAGMA against its DB; no rows are mutated, so nothing to clean up. Must not run concurrently with other callback restart/crash scenarios (same service+DB).

state_check.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT CASE WHEN count(*)=2 THEN 'CORE_TABLES_PRESENT' ELSE 'CORE_TABLES_MISSING' END FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name IN ('workflow_runs','effect_grants')"
sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT CASE WHEN count(*)=0 THEN 'FK_CLEAN' ELSE 'FK_DIRTY' END FROM pragma_foreign_key_check"

persisted_state_checks.name: no orphan rows after restart
persisted_state_checks.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT CASE WHEN count(*)=0 THEN 'FK_CLEAN' ELSE 'FK_DIRTY' END FROM pragma_foreign_key_check"

scenarios.title: Ungraceful stop mid-flight leaves no partially applied workflow
scenarios.purpose: Exercise 'a failed write leaves no partially applied workflow': stop the callback process abruptly and restart it, then confirm WAL recovery yields a consistent store with no orphaned checkpoint witness (a witness with no grant is a half-applied authorization).
scenarios.rationale: A crash between the witness insert and the grant mint (or before commit) is exactly the partial-apply hazard the AC forbids; an ungraceful stop+start is the closest reproducible trigger available.
scenarios.generating_risk: An interrupted/failed write could persist a witness without its grant, or otherwise a half-applied workflow.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-P5-1: a failed write leaves no partially applied workflow
scenarios.isolation_note: Stops then starts the shared callback service and runs read-only SELECT/PRAGMA; no data mutated. Serialize with other callback restart/crash scenarios.

state_check.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT CASE WHEN count(*)=0 THEN 'FK_CLEAN' ELSE 'FK_DIRTY' END FROM pragma_foreign_key_check"

sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT CASE WHEN count(*)=0 THEN 'ORPHAN_NONE' ELSE 'ORPHAN_FOUND' END FROM checkpoint_witnesses w WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM effect_grants g WHERE g.tenant=w.tenant AND g.grant_id=w.grant_id)"

persisted_state_checks.name: no witness without its grant after crash+recovery
persisted_state_checks.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT CASE WHEN count(*)=0 THEN 'ORPHAN_NONE' ELSE 'ORPHAN_FOUND' END FROM checkpoint_witnesses w WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM effect_grants g WHERE g.tenant=w.tenant AND g.grant_id=w.grant_id)"

persisted_state_checks.name: durable db consistent after ungraceful stop

scenarios.title: Rebuild after restart does not create a second commitment for one effect
scenarios.purpose: Exercise 'rebuilding state from history never re-executes an effect': after a restart (state re-derived from durable history), confirm the ledger still holds at most one live-or-committed grant per (tenant, commit_key) and at most one CLAIMED grant per effect.
scenarios.rationale: Re-executing an effect on rebuild would surface as a duplicate live/CLAIMED grant for the same commit_key; the live-hold and commit-once uniqueness are exactly the durable guards this AC leans on.
scenarios.generating_risk: Startup rebuild could re-run an already-committed effect, minting a duplicate reservation/commitment.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-P5-1: rebuilding state from history never re-executes an effect
scenarios.isolation_note: Restart + read-only aggregate SELECTs against effect_grants; no mutation. Serialize with other callback restart/crash scenarios.

state_check.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT CASE WHEN count(*)=0 THEN 'LIVE_UNIQUE' ELSE 'LIVE_DUP' END FROM (SELECT tenant,commit_key FROM effect_grants WHERE state IN ('GRANTED','CLAIMED') GROUP BY tenant,commit_key HAVING count(*)>1)"

sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT CASE WHEN count(*)=0 THEN 'CLAIMED_ONCE' ELSE 'CLAIMED_DUP' END FROM (SELECT tenant,commit_key FROM effect_grants WHERE state='CLAIMED' GROUP BY tenant,commit_key HAVING count(*)>1)"

persisted_state_checks.name: one live-or-committed grant per effect after rebuild
persisted_state_checks.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT CASE WHEN count(*)=0 THEN 'LIVE_UNIQUE' ELSE 'LIVE_DUP' END FROM (SELECT tenant,commit_key FROM effect_grants WHERE state IN ('GRANTED','CLAIMED') GROUP BY tenant,commit_key HAVING count(*)>1)"

persisted_state_checks.name: effect claimed at most once after rebuild
persisted_state_checks.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT CASE WHEN count(*)=0 THEN 'CLAIMED_ONCE' ELSE 'CLAIMED_DUP' END FROM (SELECT tenant,commit_key FROM effect_grants WHERE state='CLAIMED' GROUP BY tenant,commit_key HAVING count(*)>1)"

scenarios.title: Witness-to-grant stays 1:1 across a restart-driven rebuild
scenarios.purpose: Exercise 'rebuilding state from history never re-executes an effect' from the witness side: after restart, every checkpoint-minted grant has exactly one witness and no grant has two witnesses, so a replay cannot fabricate a second authorized effect.
scenarios.rationale: The kernel's contract is witness:grant = 1:1; a rebuild that duplicated or dropped a witness would either re-authorize or orphan an effect, both violations of the AC.
scenarios.generating_risk: Rebuild could duplicate a witness (re-authorize) or leave a checkpoint-minted grant unwitnessed.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-P5-1: rebuilding state from history never re-executes an effect
scenarios.isolation_note: Restart + read-only SELECTs joining checkpoint_witnesses and effect_grants; no mutation. Serialize with other callback restart/crash scenarios.

state_check.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT CASE WHEN count(*)=0 THEN 'ALL_WITNESSED' ELSE 'UNWITNESSED_GRANT' END FROM effect_grants g WHERE g.checkpoint_id IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM checkpoint_witnesses w WHERE w.tenant=g.tenant AND w.grant_id=g.grant_id)"

sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT CASE WHEN count(*)=0 THEN 'WITNESS_UNIQUE' ELSE 'WITNESS_DUP' END FROM (SELECT tenant,grant_id FROM checkpoint_witnesses GROUP BY tenant,grant_id HAVING count(*)>1)"

persisted_state_checks.name: every checkpoint-minted grant has a witness
persisted_state_checks.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT CASE WHEN count(*)=0 THEN 'ALL_WITNESSED' ELSE 'UNWITNESSED_GRANT' END FROM effect_grants g WHERE g.checkpoint_id IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM checkpoint_witnesses w WHERE w.tenant=g.tenant AND w.grant_id=g.grant_id)"

persisted_state_checks.name: no grant carries two witnesses after rebuild
persisted_state_checks.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT CASE WHEN count(*)=0 THEN 'WITNESS_UNIQUE' ELSE 'WITNESS_DUP' END FROM (SELECT tenant,grant_id FROM checkpoint_witnesses GROUP BY tenant,grant_id HAVING count(*)>1)"

assumptions: At run time the callback service is up and bound to data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 (the exact DB named in the approved sqlite3 command); the repo does not contain this file, so its existence and contents are provided by the harness, not by me.

The driver_probe workspace holds REPRESENTATIVE seeded workflow state (at least some workflow_runs, and ideally minted grants + witnesses). If it is empty, S2-S5 pass vacuously and prove far less; a seeded store is required for these invariants to be load-bearing.

The installed sqlite3 supports table-valued pragma access (pragma_foreign_key_check) and CASE-wrapped subqueries; used so the oracle emits a fixed sentinel string ('FK_CLEAN', 'CLEAN', etc.) rather than a count I cannot predict.

restart_service / stop_service+start_service on 'callback' restart the process bound to the durable DB without deleting or reinitializing it (an on-disk SQLite file survives the process); this is what makes them a genuine restart/crash test rather than a reset.

GRANT live-hold states are 'GRANTED' and 'CLAIMED' and the canonical effect_grants schema exposes tenant, commit_key, state, checkpoint_id, grant_id columns (read from src/freight_recon/workflow.py and checkpoint.py).
unresolved_questions: I was not given the builder's actual diff for U-P5-1, so I cannot target the specific 'in-process cache' that was moved. The current tree already persists workflow_runs/effect_grants/checkpoint_witnesses in SQLite; which cache the unit replaces (e.g. a per-process handle key, an operation/pending-write cache, or a run-state memo) is unknown and would sharpen every scenario.

AC 'a read after a write never returns stale state' is NOT covered by an executable scenario. Verifying it requires performing a write and then a read and comparing — but every write path (/actions/signed, /email/action, /slack/*) requires an HMAC/Slack signing secret, and there is no approved command to mint a signed token or seed a run. Please expose either a seed/fixture command that creates a workflow run and mutates it, or a loopback write endpoint that does not need the signing secret, so read-after-write and a concurrent write/read race can be exercised.

There is no approved way for me to establish a known 'before' state and assert the identical value 'after' a restart; my restart scenarios therefore assert integrity + structural invariants rather than value-level survival of a specific run. A seed command plus a read command that echoes a run's state would let me author a true write->restart->read-equals-before scenario for AC1.

Should driver_probe be seeded before this wave runs? If the harness can guarantee at least one run in each of RECEIVED/EXTRACTED/RECONCILED/NEEDS_REVIEW and at least one CLAIMED grant with its witness, S2-S5 become non-vacuous; without that guarantee they mostly confirm 'empty store stays consistent'.

Confirm the exact set of GRANT_STATES and whether any legacy (checkpoint_id IS NULL) grants may legitimately lack a witness; S5 already restricts to checkpoint_id IS NOT NULL to avoid flagging legacy legacy-owned rows, but the canonical state list should be verified against migrations/phase2_tenant_first.GRANT_STATES.
